set.reason: Sphere centers and positive radii are the meanings used in every external, internal or plane contact equation. That shared sphere-element content is necessary. Cylinder/cone/prism classifications are not necessary. The fresh R>r internal-contact endpoint leaves this narrow necessity intact.
set.scope: Interpret sphere centers and positive radii in the contact equations.

criteria: Translate external contact into a radius-sum equation, and internal contact of a smaller sphere inside a larger one into a radius-difference equation; coincident equal spheres are not a tangency case.
Translate sphere-plane contact into the perpendicular center distance equal to the radius, retaining the chosen side of the plane.
Use center geometry to recover a requested height, separation or radius, distinguishing a center height from the top of a sphere.
set.description: For R>r>0, internal sphere contact has d=R-r; external contact of positive radii has d=R+r. Sphere-plane contact has perpendicular center distance r. Keep containment and plane-side conditions.
